new_content.title: Signed Numbers: Reading Signs and Adding
new_content.intro: A signed number is a number with a plus or minus sign in front, like +4 or -4. In this lesson you will learn what the sign means on a number line, then two rules for adding signed numbers.

sections.heading: What the sign tells you
sections.body: Rule: the sign tells you which direction from zero the number sits. Positive numbers are to the right of zero, negative numbers are to the left, and the bigger the size after the sign, the farther from zero it is. So -4 sits four steps left of zero, and +4 sits four steps right of it. Two numbers like +4 and -4 are the same distance from zero but in opposite directions.
sections.example: -2 is two steps left of zero. +2 is two steps right of zero. Between -2 and +2, the one farther left is -2, so -2 is the smaller number.

sections.heading: Adding numbers with the same sign
sections.body: Rule: when both numbers have the same sign, add their sizes and keep that sign. The sizes just stack in the same direction. This works for two positives and for two negatives.
sections.example: -4 + -3. Both signs are negative, so add the sizes: 4 + 3 = 7. Keep the negative sign, so -4 + -3 = -7. For two positives, 4 + 3 = 7 the same way, giving +7.

sections.heading: Adding numbers with different signs
sections.body: Rule: when the signs differ, subtract the smaller size from the larger size, then keep the sign of the number with the larger size. One number pulls right and the other pulls left, so part of the move cancels out. The bigger pull decides the final sign.
sections.example: -6 + 4. The signs differ, so subtract the sizes: 6 - 4 = 2. The larger size is 6, which belongs to -6, so keep the negative sign. The answer is -2.

steps: Take the first two numbers, -9 and 5. Their signs differ, so use the different-sign rule.
Subtract the smaller size from the larger size: 9 - 5 = 4.
The larger size is 9, and it belongs to -9, so the result keeps the negative sign: -9 + 5 = -4.
Now add -4 + (-2). The signs are the same, so use the same-sign rule.
Add the sizes: 4 + 2 = 6, and keep the negative sign.

common_mistakes: Adding the sizes when the signs differ. For -6 + 4, adding 6 + 4 gives 10 (or -10), but the different-sign rule says subtract: 6 - 4 = 2, giving -2.
Subtracting the sizes when the signs are the same. For -4 + -3, writing -1 comes from subtracting 4 - 3, but the same-sign rule says add the sizes: 4 + 3 = 7, giving -7.
Dropping the negative sign after adding two negatives. For -4 + -3, writing 7 keeps only the size; the sign must stay negative, so the answer is -7.

Picking the number closest to zero as the smaller one when signs differ. Between -6 and +2, +2 is closer to zero, but -6 is the smaller number because a negative number is always less than a positive number.
new_content.summary: The sign of a number tells you which side of zero it sits on. Same signs: add the sizes and keep the sign. Different signs: subtract the smaller size from the larger, and keep the sign of the larger size.

The signs differ, so subtract the sizes 7 - 4 = 3 and keep the sign of the larger size, which is the 7 in -7, giving -3.
